The family of a man killed by a tiger at a zoo in northern England is appealing to the
public not to share video of the attack on social media. President Trump is among those
who shared it, as NPR's Lauren Frayer reports.
William Chapman's family says he suffered from significant mental illness. Last weekend,
the 23-year-old climbed over safety barriers into a tiger enclosure, and witnesses recorded
his final moments as a tiger mauled him. President Trump is among those who've shared the video,
adding a caption, "Don't ever mess with nature, President DJT." Later, he posted
an AI-generated video of himself in a similar stance as Chapman, but taming the tiger. Without
singling out Trump, Chapman's family calls such posts "deeply offensive" at an exceptionally
vulnerable time for them, and is asking the public to stop sharing the video. Lauren Frayer
and PR News London.
A small dog named Luna has been found after a month on the loose in Yellowstone National
Park, though spotted frequently, the Jack Russell Terrier evaded capture since early
September. Volunteers were able to catch the dog today, using a live trap baited with her
owner's scent using a t-shirt and a pillowcase belonging to the family. California owners
believe Luna escaped when a housekeeper accidentally let her out. This is NPR News from Washington.
